cohort: 490 women with a history of prior live birth at an Indian medical college and hospital, excluding those with prior abortions, stillbirths, nulliparity, or multiple pregnancies.
finding: Short interpregnancy intervals (<6 months) were associated with increased risk of fetal malposition, fetal growth restriction, and hypertension, while long interpregnancy intervals (≥5 years) were associated with increased risk of preterm labor, oligoamnios, gestational diabetes, and anemia.
